_comment: Two budgets in SI seconds, and they are never netted against each other. Cost and latency
are opposed -- batching buys one with the other -- so a cost improvement may not license a
latency regression, and seconds/ratchet.py keeps them as two independent floors.
Each floor holds its sample rather than a single number, because the gate judges against
the spread. A min-of-one ratchet fails on noise and then gets ignored.
WHAT THESE MEASURE, AND WHAT THEY DO NOT. There is no engine behind the interactor yet, so
every job below was answered by the gate or by the missing-weights error. This is the floor
of the path -- queue, transport layer, bus, interactor, CBOR back -- and says nothing about
a decomposition. When an engine lands these numbers are replaced, not added to, because a
floor carried across a change of what is being measured is a gate that only passes for the

excluded: One run at delay 9.050s: the endpoint scaling a worker up, which is a different
distribution from a warm one and would make the sample bimodal. Scale-from-zero is worth
its own budget and does not have one yet; folding it in here would hide both.

latency_seconds.what: One job, end to end as the caller sees it: RunPod queue delay plus execution, warm worker.

cost_seconds.what: Billed GPU seconds for one job: RunPod executionTime, which is what the endpoint charges for.
